references.text: The same command to write God's words on the doorposts and gates is repeated in Moses' second speech, emphasizing the importance of having God's words visible in the home.
The blood that was smeared on the doorposts and the upper lintel during Passover in Egypt represents an early form of marking a home's entrance with something holy.
The doorposts (mezuzot) are mentioned in connection with the blood of the Passover lamb, which protected the Israelites from the angel of death.
Proverbs encourages binding love and faithfulness around the neck and writing them on the tablet of the heart, a similar idea about keeping God's words visible and close.
Isaiah notes that the people have set their pagan signs behind the door and on the doorpost, an ironic contrast to the original command to write God's words there.
